findings.title: on_delete is hardcoded to "cancel" even though the module supports streaming pipelines
findings.explanation: Re-verified 2026-08-16: on_delete is now var.on_delete (variables.tf:189-198), validated to "cancel"/"drain" and documented that streaming jobs should use "drain". The gap this finding caught is closed for the classic job.

findings.title: google_dataflow_flex_template_job.main hardcodes on_delete = "cancel", reintroducing the exact gap HOLDEN_BP_001 already fixed for the classic job
findings.explanation: The classic job (google_dataflow_job.main.tf) was already fixed to use var.on_delete after HOLDEN_BP_001 flagged the same hardcode. This newer resource — added since that fix — has the identical hardcode: on_delete = "cancel" instead of var.on_delete. Any streaming pipeline launched via the Flex Template path (enable_streaming_engine, additional_experiments, or a template that streams) loses in-flight and buffered records on every terraform destroy or forced replacement, with no way for a caller to opt into "drain" the way they already can for the classic job. This is a case a deterministic rule catches once but a second, newer resource can silently reintroduce — worth a permanent policy, not just a one-off fix (see suggested_policies).
findings.remediation: Change on_delete = "cancel" to on_delete = var.on_delete, matching google_dataflow_job.main.

findings.title: google_dataflow_flex_template_job.main doesn't wire five of the module's own job-behavior variables — they silently apply to the classic job only
findings.explanation: google_dataflow_flex_template_job supports parameters, additional_experiments, enable_streaming_engine, skip_wait_on_job_termination, and transform_name_mapping as top-level arguments (confirmed against the google-beta provider schema) — the same five arguments the classic job already wires from var.parameters, var.additional_experiments, var.enable_streaming_engine, var.skip_wait_on_job_termination, and var.transform_name_mapping. None of the five are set on the Flex Template job. A caller who sets, say, var.parameters or var.enable_streaming_engine expecting it to apply module-wide gets it silently applied only to the classic job — the Flex Template job runs with no runtime parameters at all and never enables Streaming Engine, with no error or warning anywhere.
findings.remediation: Add parameters = var.parameters, additional_experiments = var.additional_experiments, enable_streaming_engine = var.enable_streaming_engine, skip_wait_on_job_termination = var.skip_wait_on_job_termination, and transform_name_mapping = var.transform_name_mapping to google_dataflow_flex_template_job.main, matching google_dataflow_job.main's own wiring.
findings.fix:
parameters                   = var.parameters
  transform_name_mapping       = var.transform_name_mapping
  additional_experiments       = var.additional_experiments
  enable_streaming_engine      = var.enable_streaming_engine
  skip_wait_on_job_termination = var.skip_wait_on_job_termination

findings.title: google_data_pipeline_pipeline.main's environment block doesn't wire machine_type, additional_experiments, enable_streaming_engine, or labels, and its launch_parameters doesn't wire parameters
findings.explanation: Confirmed against the provider schema: launch_parameters supports a parameters map (var.parameters, never set), and its nested environment block supports machine_type, additional_experiments, enable_streaming_engine, and additional_user_labels — none of which the module wires from var.machine_type, var.additional_experiments, var.enable_streaming_engine, or var.labels. Same root cause as HOLDEN_BP_003 in the sibling Flex Template job resource: a scheduled pipeline run silently ignores machine sizing, experiment flags, Streaming Engine, labels, and any runtime parameters that a caller configured expecting them to apply module-wide.
findings.remediation: In the environment block, add machine_type = var.machine_type, additional_experiments = var.additional_experiments, enable_streaming_engine = var.enable_streaming_engine, and additional_user_labels = var.labels. In launch_parameters, add parameters = var.parameters.
findings.fix:
launch_parameters {
        job_name   = "${var.name}-scheduled"
        parameters = var.parameters

        environment {
          temp_location            = var.temp_gcs_location
          kms_key_name             = var.kms_key_name
          ip_configuration         = "WORKER_IP_PRIVATE"
          network                  = var.network
          subnetwork               = var.subnetwork
          service_account_email    = google_service_account.dataflow.email
          machine_type             = var.machine_type
          max_workers              = var.max_workers
          additional_experiments   = var.additional_experiments
          enable_streaming_engine  = var.enable_streaming_engine
          additional_user_labels   = var.labels
        }
      }
